A tiny app.
A thoughtful job.

Built for the moments between
“working on it” and “over to you.”

01

Lives where a glance can find it.

Open Buddy on your Mac. Connect Claude Code with local hooks, after reviewing the change. Existing settings get a backup.

macOS 15+
02

Knows when it’s your turn.

See sessions, answer questions, review plans, and decide on permission requests. Buddy never makes an approval decision for you. You can explicitly choose an auto-accept-edits mode when approving a plan. No answer? Claude asks in the terminal as usual.

You’re in charge
03

A little further from your desk.

Step away and Buddy comes along on your iPhone. A notification shows what Claude wants; long-press it to answer a question or allow a short command, right there. Send Claude your next instruction from the phone, and it appears in the terminal as your own prompt. Everything travels through your own private iCloud, never through our servers.

iPhone companion
04

Keeps going while you’re away.

Your Mac stays awake while Claude works and waits on you, then rests ten minutes after things go quiet. Each session on your phone shows its latest prompt and reply, so you always know where it stopped.

Stays awake

A few human questions.

Does Buddy write the code?

Claude Code does the coding. Buddy is the companion that keeps activity and decisions close. The scenes above are browser illustrations, not a live connection to your computer.

What about Codex and other AI agents?

Claude Code is supported today. Codex and other agents are planned, but are not included yet. See the multi-agent roadmap.

How do I install it?

Download Buddy for Mac below, open it, and it walks you through connecting Claude Code. It shows you the change to your Claude Code settings before writing anything, and keeps a backup. The iPhone companion is coming to the App Store; the source is open on GitHub. Read the installation guide.

Do I need an iPhone?

No. The Mac app works on its own. The iPhone companion adds alerts, answers and messages for when you step away; it uses your private iCloud, signed in with the same Apple Account as your Mac. Read about the security model.
